title: GabeChoice: Agentic Steam Recommendations with LangGraph + Claude
subtitle: A personal tool that builds a taste profile from play history and ranks wishlist picks with blended LLM and Metacritic scoring

sourceDocuments.title: GabeChoice README
sourceDocuments.body: GabeChoice is a personal agentic Steam recommendation tool. It reads your library and wishlist, builds a taste profile from your play history, and produces ranked recommendations with LLM-generated reasoning. Features: parallel Steam fetching (library and wishlist concurrently), SQLite enrichment cache with genres, tags, Metacritic scores cached per-appid, 5-signal taste profile (recently played, top played, owned unplayed, wishlisted, trending), blended scoring (70% LLM taste-fit + 30% Metacritic quality), recent-play awareness (games in last 2 weeks are strongest signal), provider-agnostic LLM (Anthropic default or OpenAI), CLI and web frontend. Known limitations: Metacritic coverage ~60-75%, cold cache takes ~15 min for 400+ games, LLM latency 20-60s depending on library size.

sourceDocuments.title: GabeChoice Build Spec (SPEC.md)
sourceDocuments.body: LangGraph pipeline: fetch_library and fetch_wishlist run in parallel. enrich_games hits Steam appdetails API with SQLite cache (30-day TTL, token-bucket rate limiter at 0.5 req/s). build_taste_profile is an LLM node taking top 20 most-played games and returning a structured TasteProfile with preferred genres, mechanics, vibes, and anti-patterns. rank_and_explain is an LLM node that blends LLM taste-fit (70%) with Metacritic (30%) and writes a 1-2 sentence rationale per game. Tech stack: Python 3.12, uv, Pydantic v2, LangGraph, httpx (async), FastAPI, SQLite, Anthropic SDK and OpenAI SDK behind a thin provider abstraction, vanilla JS frontend. 24 tests covering cache, Steam client, and full pipeline with mocked clients.

sections.title: Your library. Your taste. GabeN's blessing.

blocks.text: GabeChoice is a personal agentic recommender that reads your Steam library and wishlist, builds a taste fingerprint from your play history, and ranks your wishlist with LLM reasoning blended with Metacritic scores — all running locally against your own API keys.

Steam wishlists grow faster than they shrink. Generic store recommendations ignore playtime patterns. GabeChoice turns your own play history into a taste profile, then applies it to your wishlist — no external service, no account creation, no sharing your data.
Five nodes orchestrated by LangGraph. Library and wishlist fetches run in parallel. Enrichment uses a SQLite cache so reruns skip the slow Steam API calls.

The LLM analyses the top 20 most-played games and returns a structured taste profile: preferred genres, mechanics, vibes (e.g. atmospheric, competitive, cozy), and anti-patterns. The profile is shown in the UI so the user can see and validate what the system thinks of their taste.

Provider abstraction makes Anthropic and OpenAI interchangeable with no changes to graph logic. Metacritic coverage is ~60–75% — games without scores are still ranked on taste fit alone. Cold-cache first run can take ~15 min for 400+ game libraries.
